B.name: bin1000_integer
B.prompt: Locate the object described below in the image. Description: {question} Answer with the bounding box as integer coordinates [x1, y1, x2, y2] in the 0-1000 range, where 1000 corresponds to the image width or height.
B.parse_for_metrics: frozen src.eval.grounding.parse_box; it already divides integers in [0,1000] by 1000
B.evaluator_dependency: prompt variant p1_bin1000 must be added by eval-keeper; metric code unchanged

C.name: pixel_xyxy
C.prompt: Locate the object described below in the image. Description: {question} Answer with the bounding box as pixel coordinates [x1, y1, x2, y2] using the image width and height.
C.answer_encoding: dataset raw_bbox pixel integers (x1,y1,x2,y2); validated against width/height
C.parse_for_metrics: independent conversion required: parse pixel ints, validate 0<=x1<x2<=width and 0<=y1<y2<=height, divide by width/height, then use frozen metric functions (iou/Acc@0.5/mIoU/parse semantics unchanged)
C.evaluator_dependency: prompt variant p1_pixel + pixel->normalized conversion must be implemented by eval-keeper; frozen metric code must not be changed; trainer cannot modify src/eval

cpu_tests.new_test: test_20_coordinate_representation_variants verifies prompt/encode/parse consistency for A/B/C, B evaluator-parseable roundtrip <=0.0005, C pixel conversion exactly matches GT, C boundary/ordering rejection, and that C must not be scored through the frozen parser directly

implementation.notes: read-only imports from src/eval grounding/prompts; trainer never modifies frozen evaluator files

evaluator_coordination.B: eval-keeper adds prompt variant p1_bin1000; metric parser unchanged
evaluator_coordination.C: eval-keeper adds prompt variant p1_pixel AND an independent pixel->normalized conversion layer before the frozen metric functions; metric semantics (Acc@0.5=IoU>=0.5, mIoU, parse_rate, invalid in denominator) unchanged; conversion must reject out-of-bounds/reversed boxes; spec/test oracle is src/train/coordinate_variants.py
evaluator_coordination.independence: official G4 metrics remain eval-keeper-owned; trainer only supplies training-side encoding and a CPU conversion specification/test oracle
